references.text: Deuteronomy repeats the list of unclean birds, including the raven and all its kinds, as part of the kosher laws for the people of Israel.
Ravens brought bread and meat to the prophet Elijah at the brook Cherith, showing God's use of this unclean bird to provide for His servant.
God asks Job who provides food for the raven, highlighting God's care for all creatures, including the unclean birds.
The psalm praises God who gives food to the animals and to the young ravens that cry out, emphasizing God's provision for all creation.
Isaiah prophesies about Edom's destruction where ravens will dwell, using unclean birds as a symbol of judgment and desolation.
Jesus points to the ravens, which neither sow nor reap, yet are fed by God, to teach His disciples about God's care and to discourage worry.
